topic: Negative answers to Ta's three-invariant and strict-bound questions and a proof of Conjecture 5.13 for a linear quandle family
title: Negative answers to Ta's Problems 11.6–11.7 (arXiv:2505.08090v5, Section 11, page 27) and a proof of Conjecture 5.13 (arXiv:2508.16772v1, Section 5.2.2, page 17): central-twist counting extending Kamada–Oshiro (2009), Ta (2025), and Nakajima–Yamaguchi (2026)

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We answer negatively Ta's Problems 11.6–11.7 in arXiv:2505.08090v5, Section 11, page 27, and prove his Conjecture 5.13 in arXiv:2508.16772v1, Section 5.2.2, page 17, extending the counting methods of Kamada–Oshiro (2009), Ta (2025), and Nakajima–Yamaguchi (2026). The two semidirect products C16 semidirect C4 with actions 5 and 7 have invariant triple (64,4,22), but respectively 8847360 and 2160000 good involutions. Ta's central-label characterization gives a weighted-involution formula for every finite conjugation subquandle and an exact criterion for equality in the central-label bound. The quaternion example attains that bound with two orbits and a center of order two. Inversion-closure is distinguished from classwise inverse stability, correcting Remark 2.14. For the linear quandle Lambda_(4n,2n-1), the number of good involutions is ten for odd n and four for even n; the odd case proves Conjecture 5.13, and the even case reproves Ta's Remark 5.14.
summary: An explicit equal-invariant pair answers Problem 11.6 negatively; a quaternion realization of the known R4 count answers Problem 11.7 negatively. Weighted counting extends Ta's orbit-involution method to central-twist weights and yields an exact equality criterion and a sharper whole-group bound. The cross-referenced Conjecture 5.13 is proved, and its known even companion is reproved; complete written proofs and finite checks accompany the results.

coverage.Problem 11.6: Answered: no; equal triples (64,4,22) and unequal complete counts
coverage.Problem 11.7: Answered: no; the full bound min(8,2^2)=4 is attained
coverage.Problems 11.1–11.3 and 11.5: Explicit quaternion instances; the R4 good maps reprove Kamada–Oshiro (2009), Theorem 3.2(3)
coverage.Conjectures 11.8–11.9: Prior counterexamples cited: Nakajima–Yamaguchi (2026), Example 6.8 and following paragraph
coverage.Remark 2.14: Refuted-and-corrected: inversion permutes the contained conjugacy classes, rather than fixing each class
coverage.arXiv:2508.16772v1, Lemma 5.10 and Theor: Prior method cited: weighted orbit involutions and parity factorization; extended here to general central-twist weights
coverage.arXiv:2508.16772v1, Section 5.2.2, Conje: Proved: ten good involutions for every odd n>=3; n=1 is an additional case not posed there
coverage.arXiv:2508.16772v1, Remark 5.14, page 17: Reproved; prior proof Ta (2025): four good involutions for every even positive n
